chapter: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
title: Forming the Six Nola Jazz and the Dixieland Rompers
summary: He recalls his first band, its members, and the name change to Dixieland Rompers, first to broadcast live.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And then played all the acts and everything else, you know? Mm-hmm. But he played good drums, and, and they had, uh, Kid René had a good drummer, too. I used to go and follow the bands all around, all these private parties, and every once in a while they let me sit in. When I first started to play it, I was playing pretty good then. Mm-hmm. That's when we formed the, uh, the Six Nola Jazz with Figgie Gerbick and Al Stratagas, and Eddie Powers on saxophone. And then we had Hal Maranto played piano first. Mm-hmm. Later on, Hal started to pick up Clarence and say, and we got Frank Watson, Harold-

Yeah. I didn't know that. He played wonderful clarinet. I never heard him play clarinet. Sure. Well he died now. Then we had Frank Mutz on piano. And that band, we changed the name from the Six Nola Jazzes, or New Orleans, Liliana Jazzes, we changed the name to the Dixieland Romers. And according to time, we were the first band to broadcast live on the old Crystal sets, radios, the Dixieland Romers.
